title: What is a remainder in division?
examples: Can a remainder be bigger than the number I divide by?

explain.say: Aisha has 13 stickers and wants to put them in groups of 4. Will it work out exactly? Look at the number line. We hop back from 13 in jumps of 4, taking away 12 in all, and we land on 1, not 0!

draw.text: What is a remainder in division?

explain.say: First hop: take away 4, from 13 back to 9. One group made! See the jump? Is there enough left for another group?
Second hop, from 9 back to 5. Two groups made, so 8 of the 13 stickers are used, and 5 are left. Is that still enough for one more group of 4?

Third hop, from 5 to 1. Now only 1 sticker is left, too few for another group of 4. We took away 12 in all. The 1 left over is called the remainder. So 13 divided by 4 is 3, remainder 1. Can you see the gap between 1 and 0?

Brilliant! Check it: 3 groups of 4 make 12, and the 1 left makes 13. A remainder is always smaller than the group size. Real life: 13 children going in cars of 4 need 4 cars, so nobody is left behind!

faq.a: A remainder is what is left over when a number cannot be split exactly. 13 in groups of 4 makes 3 groups with 1 left over, so the remainder is 1.
13 divided by 4 is 3 remainder 1. Three groups of 4 make 12, and 1 is left over.

faq.q: Can a remainder be bigger than the number I divide by?
faq.a: No. If the leftover is as big as a group or bigger, you can make another group. When you divide by 4, the remainder can only be 0, 1, 2 or 3.
asks: Can the remainder be more than the group size?

faq.q: How do I write a remainder?
faq.a: Write r and the leftover after the answer. 13 divided by 4 is written 3 r 1.
asks: What does r mean in division?

faq.q: What do I do with a remainder in a word problem?
faq.a: Think about the story. 13 children in cars of 4 need 4 cars, so you round up. But 13 sweets in bags of 4 fill only 3 full bags, so the spare sweet does not count.
asks: Do I round up or down?

facts: When you divide by 4, the remainder can only be 0, 1, 2 or 3.

quiz.why: 3 fives are 15, and 2 are left over: 3 r 2.

wrong.2: 4 fives are 20, which is more than 17.

quiz.say: When you divide by 3, which remainder is impossible?
quiz.show: When you divide by 3, which remainder is impossible?
quiz.why: A leftover of 3 is enough for another group of 3, so it cannot be the remainder.

wrong.0: A remainder of 1 is possible: 7 ÷ 3 = 2 r 1.
wrong.1: A remainder of 2 is possible: 8 ÷ 3 = 2 r 2.
